name: site-footer
description: Footer for customer/content-facing Woodfine/PointSav sites (as distinct from machine-surface-footer, which serves developer-facing tool sites like design.pointsav.com). Composes a brand re-anchor block (top), a free-form context slot (site-specific columns, hand-authored per site), a network slot, an optional disclosure block driven by a named legal-tokens disclaimer profile, and a fixed identity bar (locations/badge/copyright/disclaimer/trademark — byte-identical across every site that uses this component, except the two fields documented as expected to vary).
stub_source: project-editorial footer/badge architecture research — BRIEF-footer-badge-token-architecture.md (2026-07-10); reconciled 2026-07-12 with project-marketing's live mobile-audit findings on home.woodfinegroup.com/home.pointsav.com; revised 2026-07-16 to a mandatory/recommended/site's-choice tiering following a full live audit of all 8 Woodfine/PointSav sites (5 distinct footer implementations found, not 2) plus external research into GOV.UK Design System, Wikimedia Foundation, and Stripe precedent for where multi-property design systems actually draw the 'must match' line — see notes field and the tiering block below. project-knowledge has self-certified as content-steward of this component subtree per conventions/token-stewardship-by-domain.md; project-design retains sole commit authority.

tiering.mandatory: Legal/trademark identity + structural contract only, per GOV.UK/Wikimedia/Stripe precedent (the only layer real multi-property systems lock across independently-run properties). A customer/investor-facing footer must include a trademark/copyright block sourced byte-verbatim from the canonical legal-tokens-{brand}.yaml (factory-release-engineering, admin-tier) — recipe.json references that file as the source of truth and never embeds its own copy of the trademark text; a third copy is exactly the drift risk that produced a 3-live-variant trademark-statement bug (flagged separately to Command, admin-tier fix, not part of this component). A site with no customer/investor audience (e.g. design.pointsav.com, a pure tooling/reference site) may formally declare an audience exemption from the legal block entirely — this is already how design.pointsav.com behaves today (no trademark-list block, no legal-disclosure accordion), confirmed correct, not a defect.
tiering.recommended: A starter palette (not enforced) — 3 visual values already implemented and verified in app-mediakit-knowledge (--k-shadow-footer, --k-text-footer-heading, --k-leading-relaxed) any site may copy into its own local token file; no cross-site token pipeline exists today, each site's session encodes its own copy. Plus one new named variant: footer.high-risk-transaction — a persistent, always-visible one-line disclaimer strip layered above a collapsed legal-disclosure accordion, software.pointsav.com's own live pattern, justified for sites handling irreversible transactions (a warning gated behind a <details> toggle may never be seen). Documented as opt-in, crediting software.pointsav.com as the origin.
tiering.sites_choice:
Typography scale, spacing rhythm, color, elevation, column count/grouping, separator glyph, and disclosure UX (accordion vs. persistent strip vs. none) are all legitimately site-adaptable per every external precedent found. bim.woodfinegroup.com's richer editorial columns, 'Machine-readable surface' API-links column, pipe separator, and implicit

-stacked base block are legitimate presentation choices for a technical-catalog audience, NOT gaps against this recipe — do not ask it to converge to this recipe's exact row/separator structure. This corrects the 2026-07-16 draft's own first version, which had implied bim.woodfinegroup.com needed to 'reach recipe compliance'.

variants.name: footer.high-risk-transaction
variants.description: A persistent, always-visible one-line disclaimer strip layered above a collapsed legal-disclosure accordion — for sites handling irreversible transactions. Origin: software.pointsav.com's own live pattern. Opt-in, see tiering.recommended.
variants.status: recommended, not yet implemented as a distinct recipe fragment

slots.name: siteName / tagline
slots.authored: siteName is the site's own brand name; tagline reuses the same one-line canonical description already used for the site's own SEO meta description / JSON-LD description field — deliberately not a second hand-authored copy, to avoid a second copy drifting out of sync with the first.
slots.description: Brand re-anchor block, rendered above everything else in the footer, so brand identity is re-established once the masthead has scrolled off-screen on a long page.

slots.name: contextColumns
slots.description: BIM spec numbers, GIS data credits, machine-surface endpoint lists, version strings, etc. This component does not template or constrain this content beyond providing the layout container.

slots.name: networkLinks
slots.description: Cross-links to sibling sites in the family.

slots.name: disclosureProfile / disclosureStatements
slots.description: Which statements render is data-driven by profile name; the section shape (heading + list + full-disclaimer link) is fixed.

slots.name: locations / copyrightStatement / disclaimerOneLiner / trademarkStatement / attributionBadge
slots.authored: byte-identical, sourced from legal-tokens-*.yaml + attribution-badges.yaml, never hand-typed per site
slots.description: The fixed bottom bar. This is the layer that must never drift — every prior footer inconsistency found in the 2026-07-10 research (missing trademark notice on design.pointsav.com, pipe vs middot separator, section-heading synonyms) was a failure in this layer specifically. The badge sits right-aligned on the locations row, above its own copyright row — repositioned 2026-07-12 per a real mobile-legibility fix (see notes).

content_conventions.separator: middot (·) only — matches the family's existing convention ("v0.3.0 · live", "Apache-2.0 · platform code AGPL-3.0-or-later"). Do not use a pipe (|); the live sites' current "Vancouver | New York" is the one inconsistency this component corrects.
content_conventions.link_arrow: → (rightwards arrow) — the only inline link-continuation glyph used in footer prose.
content_conventions.section_heading_note: Fixed wording (sentence case in markup/content — do not introduce a synonym for an existing heading; prior drift found: "Family & Legal" / "Legal & Attribution" / "Corporate identity" were three names for one drawer). Rendered visually as uppercase with ~0.08em letter-spacing via CSS text-transform (see .ps-site-footer__heading) — NOT authored as literal all-caps text in the markup/content layer, so screen readers don't risk reading the heading as a letter-by-letter acronym. This supersedes the original 2026-07-10 draft's sentence-case *visual* treatment: project-marketing's 2026-07-12 live mobile audit of home.pointsav.com found a real coherence bug from mismatched casing (disclosure heading sentence-case, nav column labels uppercase+tracked) and fixed it toward uppercase+tracked — that fix is adopted here as the real, evidence-backed convention rather than the draft's untested original choice.

aria: <footer> is a landmark role (contentinfo) implicitly; should be the last landmark on the page. Section headings (h2) label each column/block for screen-reader navigation.
open_questions: Should the MANDATORY trademark-block reference mechanism (recipe.json pointing at legal-tokens-{brand}.yaml rather than embedding text) be formalized as a machine-checkable contract a site's own build.rs can validate against (closer to GOV.UK's published component API), or is documentation-only guidance sufficient given how small this site family currently is? The machine-checkable version is a bigger lift — worth a separate DESIGN-RESEARCH if judged worthwhile; the 2026-07-16 draft only proposes the documentation-only version.

Exact `{{#if}}` / templating syntax should match whatever templating convention app-mediakit-shell actually uses (maud/Rust, not literal Handlebars) — this recipe uses Handlebars-style placeholders as the design-system's existing recipes do (see machine-surface-footer), for the design system's own documentation purposes; the consuming Rust code translates it, it does not consume this JSON literally.
research_links: project-marketing mailbox message 'Proposed shared pattern — footer structure, disclosure accordion, and browser-tab tokens' (relayed via command@claude-code, 2026-07-12) — source of the brand re-anchor block, badge repositioning, and section-heading-casing reconciliation

notes: Reconciled 2026-07-12 (operator-approved) against the original 2026-07-10 draft in 3 ways, all grounded in project-marketing's real, already-shipped live-site fixes rather than invented preference: (1) section-heading casing changed from sentence-case-visual to uppercase+tracked-visual (see content_conventions.section_heading_note for the full reasoning); (2) added the brand re-anchor block (siteName + tagline) at the top of the footer, absent from the original draft; (3) repositioned the attribution badge from inline-with-locations-and-copyright to right-aligned on its own locations row, with copyright demoted to its own row below — fixes a real mobile bug (badge buried under legal text) project-marketing found and fixed on home.pointsav.com/home.woodfinegroup.com. Token references also corrected from the original draft's invented --pds-* CSS var prefix and nonexistent paths (semantic.surface.default, semantic.ink.tertiary) to this vault's real --ps-* prefix and real token names (semantic.surface-subtle, semantic.ink-disabled) — verified directly against dtcg-vault/tokens/primitive.json and dtcg-vault/themes/pointsav-brand.json before writing this file. Revised again 2026-07-21 (this commit) to fold in project-knowledge's 2026-07-16 tiering draft: added the tiering block (mandatory/recommended/site's-choice) and the footer.high-risk-transaction variant; resolved the prior open question about design.pointsav.com's adoption (it correctly uses the audience-exemption path, confirmed not a defect); corrected the framing around bim.woodfinegroup.com's footer from 'gap against this recipe' to 'legitimate site's-choice divergence'.
